findings.detail: available: handler serializes float64 (JSON number, e.g. 2450000) but spec declares type string
findings.evidence: handlers/types.go:27 (Available float64 `json:"available"`, written at handlers/accounts.go:19) vs spec BalanceResponse.available {"type": "string"}

findings.detail: ledger: handler serializes float64 (JSON number, e.g. 2500000) but spec declares type string
findings.evidence: handlers/types.go:28 (Ledger float64 `json:"ledger"`, written at handlers/accounts.go:20) vs spec BalanceResponse.ledger {"type": "string"}

findings.detail: X-Signature: handler sets an X-Signature response header that is not declared in the 202 response of the spec
findings.evidence: handlers/misc.go:60 — w.Header().Set("X-Signature", "sha256=deadbeef"); spec /webhooks/test 202 response defines no headers

findings.detail: accountNumber, bankCode, amount, currency: spec marks them required in PayoutRequest, but the handler only rejects a mis
findings.evidence: handlers/payouts.go:31-34 (only req.Reference is validated) vs spec components.schemas.PayoutRequest.required = [accountNumber, bankCode, amount, currency, reference]

findings.detail: payoutId, amount: spec marks them required in RefundRequest, but the handler performs no field validation — requests omi
findings.evidence: handlers/payouts.go:85-91 (CreateRefund decodes the body with no validation) vs spec components.schemas.RefundRequest.required = [payoutId, amount]

findings.detail: 409: spec documents 409 (duplicate reference) but no code path in CreatePayout can ever return 409
422: spec documents 422 (refund not permitted) but no code path in CreateRefund can ever return 422
404: spec documents 404 for unknown customer IDs but GetCustomer unconditionally returns 200
findings.evidence: handlers/accounts.go:97-107 — GetCustomer has no 404 branch and always calls writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, ...)
